symptom: An import mapping's custom object handler `find … by M.MF ( P: member )` that names a parameter the microflow does not declare (or the right name in another case) passed `check` and `exec` and was written; `mx check` reported CE1613 "The selected parameter 'M.MF.P' no longer exists". Naming only some of the microflow's parameters was CE0277 "Parameter mapping of microflow for obtaining objects needs to be refreshed".
file: mdl/executor/validate_mapping_handler_params.go ValidateMappingHandlerParams (MDL104), called from validate_program.go with the lazy project opener. Tests: validate_mapping_handler_params_test.go; fixtures mdl-examples/bug-tests/mapping-handler-unknown-parameter(.fail).mdl, mapping-handler-missing-parameter.fail.mdl
cause: buildCustomHandler qualifies each parameter against the microflow (`Microflow + "." + Parameter`) and never looks the name up, and nothing counts the parameters. CE0281 itself, the code this was started from, cannot be produced by hand: exec refuses a `by` member that is not in the JSON structure (addCustomHandlerValueElements), so mx check never sees it; check does not mirror that refusal and it was left alone because the mirror would duplicate the builder's JSON-path tracking.
insight: **One mapping per project when measuring a build that stages its errors: a shared project made two real errors read as clean.** My first matrix put nine mappings in one project; three were CE1613 (an unresolved reference, stage 0, which hides every other error in every document), so `Index: code` (really CE0282) and one-of-two parameters (really CE0277) both showed '-' and I wrote 'leaving a parameter out is clean' into the rule's header and a test. It surfaced only because the control fixture, applied alone, reported 1 error. Re-measured isolated: names exact and all named clean; unknown, wrong-case or extra name CE1613; one or none of the parameters named CE0277; none named on a zero-parameter microflow clean; a String member into an Integer parameter CE0282 (not covered). The two codes need two fail fixtures for the same reason: in one project CE1613 hides the CE0277. An unknown name is judged alone, as the build does. The same staging that the documented stage table already records was the trap, so run the control and every fail fixture in their own project before trusting a count. Sweep: 1,325 repo .mdl files, 0 MDL104 hits. Control: stubbing the rule fails 12 sub-tests.
